comparisons.title: Same goal. Different heating strategies.
comparisons.goal: Heat a mug and put it in a cabinet.

changes.label: Heating strategy
changes.right: Uses the microwave, then the cabinet

comparisons.interpretation: These are separate C and E evaluations of the same task instance. The microwave route appears in E's plan; the shown rule concerns navigation after heating. This pair illustrates behavior, not the isolated effect of that rule.

beats.label: Start
beats.title: One goal, the same restored scene
beats.text: Both recorded policies must heat a mug and store it in a cabinet.

beats.label: Pick up
beats.title: Both agents obtain the mug
beats.text: The difference emerges after pickup, rather than from whether the mug can be found.

beats.label: Decision
beats.title: The routes diverge
beats.text: C goes to a stoveburner. E goes to the microwave.

beats.label: Heat
beats.title: A failed placement versus a valid heating command
beats.text: C attempts an invalid placement on a stoveburner. E executes heat mug 1 with microwave 1.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.title: The outcomes separate
beats.text: C uses the full 30-action budget without heating the mug. E satisfies the goal in eight actions.

comparisons.title: Same goal. Fourteen actions versus three.
comparisons.goal: Hold the bowl with the desk lamp turned on.

changes.label: Handling the bowl
changes.left: Puts it down, then repeatedly examines the desk
changes.right: Keeps holding it and switches on the lamp

comparisons.interpretation: Both evaluations succeed on the exact same task instance. The visible difference is efficiency: C takes 11 additional actions. The simulator's goal requires holding the bowl with the lamp on; repeated examine commands are unnecessary.

beats.label: Start
beats.title: The same bowl and lamp task
beats.text: The objective is satisfied when the agent is holding the bowl and the desk lamp is on.

beats.label: Pick up
beats.title: Both pick up the bowl
beats.text: At this point both policies have the object needed for the goal.

beats.label: Decision
beats.title: C puts it down; E turns on the lamp
beats.text: E completes the task. C has put the bowl back on the desk, so turning the lamp on next is insufficient.

beats.label: Extra work
beats.title: E is finished while C keeps examining
beats.text: C repeatedly examines the desk with empty hands. E's completed replay holds its final frame.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.title: Both win, with an 11-action difference
beats.text: C eventually picks the bowl up again with the lamp already on. E reaches that state directly in three actions.

comparisons.title: Same task. A failed attempt, then a successful retry.
comparisons.goal: Find the cloth and put it in a drawer.

changes.label: Prompt context
changes.left: No reflection from this attempt yet
changes.right: Reflection on the failed search is supplied

changes.label: Rule manual during the attempt
changes.right: The manual stays fixed during the retry

comparisons.interpretation: This is a genuine chronological first-attempt/retry sequence for one practice game. Reflection is added before the retry. The Builder writes a new Success Process after the retry succeeds; that new rule did not cause this retry's win.

beats.label: Start
beats.title: The same practice game is reset
beats.text: Both attempts begin from the same task scene and need to find a cloth for the drawer.

beats.label: Reflect
beats.title: Failure produces a reflection
beats.text: The first attempt ends without finding the cloth. Its reflection is supplied when the retry starts.

beats.label: Find cloth
beats.title: The retry finds and picks up the cloth
beats.text: The retry searches several receptacles, finds the cloth at the toilet, and takes it.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.title: The retry succeeds and the Builder records a procedure
beats.text: After placing the cloth in the drawer, the Builder adds a new Success Process to the rule manual.

comparisons.title: One delivery is not enough. Complete both.
comparisons.goal: Find two tissue boxes and put both on the toilet.

changes.label: Search and delivery
changes.left: Searches drawers; completes one valid delivery
changes.right: Finds both boxes on a surface and delivers each

comparisons.interpretation: E was shown a multiple-object procedure and surface-search guidance. C delivers one box but its later invalid placement commands do not count as deliveries. The paired E record succeeds by placing two boxes on the target.

beats.label: Start
beats.title: Two objects must reach the target
beats.text: Both replays need two tissue boxes on the toilet, rather than a single successful delivery.

beats.label: Search
beats.title: Drawer search versus a surface containing both boxes
beats.text: C is still searching drawers. E goes to the countertop where the recorded observations show the tissue boxes.

beats.label: First box
beats.title: Each replay completes its first delivery
beats.text: C delivers its first box on action 12. E delivers its first on action 4.

beats.label: Second box
beats.title: Finding another box is only part of the task
beats.text: Both now hold another box. E follows through by returning to the target before placing it.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.title: E completes both deliveries
beats.text: E places the second tissue box on the toilet and satisfies the goal. C ends without a second valid delivery.

comparisons.title: Find the watch, then complete the delivery.
comparisons.goal: Find a watch and put it on the side table.

changes.label: Memory available
changes.right: Three rules from the check-d library

changes.label: Search behavior
changes.left: Revisits drawers and receptacles without finding the watch
changes.right: Checks furniture surfaces and finds the watch

comparisons.interpretation: The C and E records share a task instance. E uses the check-d library, which differs from the check-e library in other demo tabs. Its eight-action run finds the watch on the coffee table and places it on the side table. The source labels preserve this distinction.

beats.label: Start
beats.title: The same watch and side-table goal
beats.text: Both recordings start from the same restored task scene.

beats.label: Search
beats.title: E reaches the surface holding the watch
beats.text: C is opening drawers. E has checked the armchair and sofa, then reaches the coffee table.

beats.label: Pick up
beats.title: E picks up the watch
beats.text: E takes watch 1 from the coffee table. At the aligned checkpoint, C still has an empty inventory.

beats.label: Target
beats.title: Reaching the target is useful only with the object
beats.text: Both recordings reach the side table. E is carrying the watch and can complete the delivery.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.title: E completes the recorded task
beats.text: E places the watch on the side table and wins in eight actions. C does not find and deliver it within 30 actions.

comparisons.title: A success can still contain unnecessary work.
comparisons.goal: Heat a tomato and put it on the dining table.

changes.label: Memory available
changes.right: Two rules from the check-avoid70 library

changes.label: Heating behavior
changes.left: Attempts stove commands and an invalid heating command
changes.right: Eventually holds the tomato and uses the microwave correctly

changes.label: Recorded outcome
changes.right: Goal met in 23 actions, including repeated door actions

comparisons.interpretation: E's saved run succeeds but is not an optimal demonstration: it repeatedly opens and closes the microwave before taking the tomato back into its hand and issuing the valid heating command. C and E are separate runs, and this E record uses the check-avoid70 library.

beats.label: Start
beats.title: The same heating requirement
beats.text: A tomato must be heated before it is placed on the dining table.

beats.label: Find tomato
beats.title: Both find the tomato in the fridge
beats.text: Both recordings pick up tomato 3. Success depends on what happens after pickup.

beats.label: Extra work
beats.title: Neither route is a direct solution
beats.text: C attempts an invalid stove command. E is still repeating microwave door actions.

beats.label: Heat
beats.title: The heating command requires holding the object
beats.text: C's heating command is invalid after it has put the tomato down. E takes the tomato back and then heats it with the microwave.

beats.label: Outcome
beats.title: E eventually completes the task
beats.text: E places the heated tomato on the dining table. C ends its 30-action recording without satisfying the heating goal.

selection_policy: New E episodes must succeed; recorded C baselines may fail.
